Resume Keywords: What ATS Software Actually Scans For

Most "keyword stuffing" advice is wrong. ATS software doesn't reward the most keywords — it rewards the right keywords, used naturally, that match what a specific job description is actually asking for.

Resume Score CheckerJD Resume Optimizer

Where resume keywords actually come from

The single best source of keywords for any application is the job description itself — the required skills, tools, certifications and even the exact job title. ATS software is typically matching your resume text against that JD, not against some universal "best keywords" list.

  • •Required and preferred skills sections of the JD
  • •Tools, frameworks and platforms named explicitly (e.g. "Java" vs "programming languages")
  • •The exact job title and any level qualifiers ("Senior", "Lead")
  • •Certifications or qualifications mentioned as requirements

How to use them without keyword stuffing

Work each relevant keyword into a real bullet point that describes something you actually did — not a bare list at the bottom of the page. A keyword with no supporting context reads as stuffing to both ATS relevance scoring and human reviewers.

  • •Use the exact term from the JD once in a bullet, not five variations of it
  • •Match both the acronym and full form once each (e.g. "SEO" and "search engine optimization")
  • •Avoid hiding keywords in white text or tiny fonts — modern ATS and recruiters both catch this and it can get an application rejected outright

Role-specific keyword lists

Keyword needs vary enormously by role — a Data Analyst resume and a DevOps Engineer resume should not share a keyword list. See role-specific ATS keywords, skills and sample bullet points on the resume-by-role hub.

Frequently asked questions

How many keywords should a resume include?

There's no magic number — match the 8-12 most important terms from the specific job description, worked naturally into real bullet points, rather than hitting an arbitrary keyword count.
